question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
generated_answer: The SIN is a nine-digit number that you will need to work in Canada and to access government programs and benefits. You do not have to give your SIN number to your employer, but if you do, you must be given a copy of the SIN request form. You should only give your SIN number to your employer after you have been hired. If you are asked to provide your SIN number before you have been hired, you should politely decline and explain that you will provide it once you have been hired. It is important to note that providing your SIN number to your employer is not a requirement for getting a job in Canada. You have the right to refuse to provide your SIN number if you are not comfortable doing so. However, you may be asked to provide other identification, such as a driver's license or passport, in order to verify your identity and eligibility to work in Canada.
